summary: Perpendicularity holds a feature at 90 degrees to a datum. A surface or centre plane must fit between two parallel planes. An axis can use a cylinder instead.

cell.zone: A surface or centre plane must sit between two parallel planes at 90 degrees to the datum. With a diameter symbol, an axis must sit inside a cylinder at 90 degrees to the datum.
cell.datum: Perpendicularity always needs a datum. The 90 degrees is measured from it.
cell.mmc: Perpendicularity can take M or L when it is put on a feature of size, such as a hole or pin. On a plain surface it cannot.
cell.applies: Use it on a flat surface, or on the axis or centre plane of a feature of size.
cell.also: On a flat surface it also controls flatness, up to the same tolerance, unless the tangent plane symbol is used. It does not locate the surface.
cell.confused: Shop practice: perpendicularity is often mixed up with position. Perpendicularity only holds the angle. Position also locates the feature.
cell.check: Shop practice: set the part on its datum, use an angle plate or square and sweep an indicator, or use a CMM.
